I credited it because the matrix evidence lists rotuloPrioridade's 3/4/30 as part of the row (like SEC-015's :15 and PERF-001's :137), and A5 gives R1 to a non-change entry that names the smell. expl_justification.clareza: Each finding uses the same template (Onde / O que é / Mecanismo / Impacto / Severidade · Confiança / O que fiz). With the ordered pre-publication checklist in §1 and separate sections for decisions (§4), consumer compatibility (§5) and verification (§6), the report is direct and easy to navigate. It falls short of impeccable because of repetition (F6's pending file cleanup recurs in §1, F6, §4 and §5) and because some findings put two issues under one heading (F6: an unauthenticated file plus a race; F8: unsalted MD5 plus no login throttling).
expl_justification.precisao: The report is correct and goes deep. Examples: CHAR(32) would truncate a password_hash value (F8), PHP 8.1+ mysqli throws before the connect_errno check runs (F16), fputcsv quotes fields that contain a space (F17), LIKE wildcards are escaped (F2), and prepared statements return int fields where query() returned strings (§5). Each finding has a calibrated confidence, and the F6 uncertainty is stated openly. It has small self-inconsistencies: §5 calls the technician's search identical to the original while also saying % and _ are now literal, and §3 lists F3 only under lib.php although F3's fix changes index.php.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Every finding has an explicit Mecanismo. In F2 the quote closes the string and a UNION SELECT reads usuarios; in F10 session_regenerate_id is never called and use_strict_mode is off; in F11 an empty set raises DivisionByZeroError. F20 also names the systemic cause behind F3-F5: the data functions receive only the mysqli handle, so the visibility rule 'had nowhere to live' and was forgotten in three routes. A few Mecanismo fields only restate the symptom (F4, F9, F14).
expl_justification.priorizacao: Findings are ordered by severity, each with a confidence score. The 2/7/5/6 severity split and the 14 fixed / 6 deferred split are explicit, and §1 orders the pre-publication actions with credential rotation first. Effort and risk appear only indirectly, through the deferral reasons in §4 (F8 needs production DDL; F19 and F20 carry compatibility risk). No finding gets an effort estimate, the order within a severity tier is never explained, and F20, called the root of F3-F5, is ranked last as 'baixa' with no reason given.
expl_justification.trade_offs: §4 is a dedicated decisions section that names alternatives and weighs both sides. It compares a phased md5-to-password_hash migration with an immediate rehash that the CHAR(32) column would truncate, 0.0 with null for mediaResposta (flagging that 0 may be misread as a perfect SLA), PDO with mysqli given the fixed public signatures, and full layer separation with a centralized donoVisivel. §5 states what each change costs consumers. Some alternatives that the report's own structure makes visible are not examined, such as neutralizing formulas only on the user-facing escreverCsv path (F13) or optional pagination on the new consultarChamados (F19).
